text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear opening claim against driverless cars","quality":"positioning","description":"It states a definite argumentative stance right away, making the essay’s purpose immediately clear."},{"evidence":"“If companies sell driverless cars people will pay less attention to the road”","quality":"claim development","description":"It develops a central reason for its position instead of mostly listing article facts."},{"evidence":"“because they think that the car will always be reliable”","quality":"reasoning","description":"It explains how the risk of overtrust could lead to accidents, showing cause-and-effect logic."},{"evidence":"“What if you do get in an accident… whose fault will it be”","quality":"counterargument awareness","description":"It raises the liability issue from the article and uses it to strengthen the opposition."},{"evidence":"“Let’s be honest… they might just see driveless car and assume”","quality":"audience engagement","description":"It uses direct, conversational appeal to pull the reader into the argument."},{"evidence":"“People don't need to have driveless cars anyways because they need to get comfortable with driving”","quality":"concluding emphasis","description":"It ends with a broader takeaway that reinforces the writer’s overall position."}]}
